title: Wanted man killed in shootout with Sask. RCMP feared police, sister says
subtitle: Trent Angus, 33, was fatally shot during an RCMP raid on a business in Waseca on Feb. 26.
article: Lori-Anne Angus remembers her youngest brother, Trent Byron Angus, as a loving father who liked fixing and detailing vehicles and working in the shop.
Saskatchewan police knew him differently: for past charges involving firearms and for an incident in which a stolen car was used to ram an RCMP vehicle during an arrest in Lloydminster.
Trent, 33, was fatally shot in an exchange of gunfire with RCMP in Waseca on Feb. 26.

At the time, he was wanted on charges of pointing, possessing and discharging a firearm in connection with a Nov. 28 incident in which a man went to a home on Little Pine First Nation and fired a gun, hitting a parked vehicle, before fleeing.
Lori-Anne acknowledged her brother was wanted by police, but said she still wishes they had handled the situation differently.
"They could have found alternative ways to arrest him instead of having to shoot him so many times," she said in an interview.
Saskatoon city police are investigating the events of Feb. 26, including the shooting and the way next-of-kin notification was done.
Saskatchewan RCMP declined to comment, citing the ongoing investigation.
In a news release after the shooting, RCMP said a search warrant was executed at a commercial property in Waseca at 11:45 a.m. on Feb. 26, with involvement from its critical incident response team.

That search warrant was executed after police searched two homes in Lloydminster, seizing firearms, prohibited weapons, hundreds of rounds of ammunition and drugs. Two people were arrested and charged in connection with the home searches.
RCMP reported recovering items including nine firearms and hundreds of rounds of ammunition after searching three properties over the weekend.
"Based on information obtained during the investigation, officers believed there was a significant risk to public and police safety," RCMP said in a Feb. 27 news release.

Lori-Anne said Trent and her son - who was among the people taken into custody - were at the Waseca property - a mechanic shop - to fix her truck. Earlier that day, Trent spent time on Little Pine First Nation with his youngest child, she said.

According to RCMP, after three people left the building, the fourth remained inside "and was not complying with police officer commands." They say he then "exited the building and continued to not comply with police officer commands."
He displayed a firearm and gunfire was exchanged, police said at the time.
An unidentified officer who was shot in the head was treated in hospital.
"Saskatchewan RCMP's thoughts continue to be with the family of the deceased male, as well as with our injured police officer as they recover," RCMP said in a news release after the shootout.
Lori-Anne said her brother had told his family he was afraid he'd die at the hands of police.
Prior to the February incident, he had at least one major encounter with RCMP in Lloydminster.
In May 2016, RCMP said Trent rammed an RCMP vehicle with a stolen vehicle, fled on foot, broke into a home and was arrested. He was wanted on outstanding warrants at the time.
Lori-Anne said the family feels his arrest that day was unnecessarily violent; his jaw had to be wired shut after the encounter.

Alberta RCMP confirmed recently that it conducted an internal investigation into that arrest, which was reviewed by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT). The Crown reviewed its findings and did not recommend charges against the arresting officers.

Lori-Anne said her family plans to hire a lawyer to represent them in the wake of her brother's death. She said they don't trust the investigation process since it involves police investigating police.
"It's so unreal because I can't even believe it," she said.
Saskatoon police declined to comment while the investigation is ongoing.
